key_insight: HullFT speeds up test-time finetuning by selecting a small, diverse support set through convex geometry and then reusing gradients across repeated examples.
engineering_relevance: It makes per-query adaptation of LLMs more practical by reducing both retrieval overhead and finetuning cost, improving the quality–latency tradeoff.
method: Represent the query as a sparse convex combination of training sequences using Frank-Wolfe optimization.
Convert fractional convex weights into an exact integer multiset for finetuning.
Reuse gradients for repeated examples to amortize forward-backward computation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower bits-per-byte at substantially lower total runtime than current state-of-the-art TTFT methods.
watch_item: The approach depends on efficient retrieval, convex optimization, and careful integerization, so implementation complexity and approximation quality may affect real-world gains.
paper_title: Efficient Test-Time Finetuning of LLMs via Convex Reconstruction and Gradient Caching
